Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred against the award of the Tribunal dated 10.01.2025 passed in MVC No.426/2023 by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Shivamogga,
sitting at Sagar (for short 'Tribunal').
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Sri Dayananda S/o of Subramani met with an accident on 04.01.2023 and died subsequently.
His wife and son filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.95,50,000/- with interest.
But the Tribunal considered the entire evidence on record and granted Rs.19,89,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from date of petition till realisation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellants have preferred this appeal.
3. Learned counsel for appellants mainly contented that Dayananda was working as a photographer and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.

But the Tribunal has taken his income as Rs.16,000/- per month and 40% NC: 2026:KHC:13455 HC-KAR towards future prospects is not added while calculating the loss of dependency as per the citation reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others and meager compensation was granted under the conventional heads.
Interest has to be granted at the rate of 9%.

Therefore,
requested for enhancement of the compensation.

4. Heard learned counsels on both sides.
5.
The claimants before the Tribunal have not filed any income proof of Dayananda.
As he met with an accident in the year 2023, Tribunal has rightly considered his notional income as Rs.16,000/- as per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
He was aged 38 years and the multiplier is 15.
He is entitled for 40% towards future prospects and 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Hence, loss of dependency comes to Rs.26,88,000/-
(16,000+40%x12x15-1/3).

The first petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/- towards spousal consortium and second NC: 2026:KHC:13455 HC-KAR petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/-
towards parental consortium and they are also entitled for Rs.33,000 under the conventional heads.
6. Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is re-
assessed as follows;
Particulars Rs. Amount
Loss of dependency Rs. 26,88,000.00  Loss of consortium Rs. 88,000.00
Conventional heads Rs. 33,000.00  Total compensation Rs. 28,09,000.00

Bhagya S vs Khaleel Ahammad on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/223136/
3  7.
The compensation is enhanced from Rs.19,89,900/- to Rs.28,09,000/-.
The appellants are entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.8,19,100/- along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the petition, till its actual realization.

8. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed.
NC: 2026:KHC:13455 HC-KAR 2.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and re-assessed as indicated above.
3. The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit enhanced compensation amount of Rs.8,19,100/-with interest at the rate of 6 % p.a., within a period of one month from the date of this order.
4. On such deposit, the first petitioner/wife of the deceased alone is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the accrued interest.
5. Claimants are not entitled for interest for delay period of 102 days as per order in IA.No.1/2025 dated 05.03.2026.
Draw the award accordingly.

Sd/-
